title: Fire by Night
subtitle: Leviticus & Numbers in Poems & Pictures
beforeYouBegin:
Leviticus and Numbers are the books of the camp at Sinai and the long road after it. They hold a fire on the altar that must never go out, a handful of flour seasoned with salt, a goat walking alone into the desert, corners of a field left standing for the poor, and a horn that sounds liberty every fiftieth year. Then the camp sets out: a blessing spoken over the people, a cloud by day and fire by night, manna in the dew, a cluster of grapes carried on a pole, a dry rod covered in almond blossoms, water pouring from a rock, a donkey that stops in the road, and six cities with their gates open for anyone who needs to run.

This book walks through them in forty short poems, in five parts: two for Leviticus and three for Numbers. Each poem sits beside a picture and under a single line of Scripture.

The poems are not the Bible. They are one reader's response to it. Open the books of Leviticus and Numbers alongside this book, and let the real words have the last word.

parts.title: Part One · The Fire on the Altar
parts.epigraph: Fire shall be kept burning on the altar continually; it shall not go out.

parts.title: Part Two · I Will Walk Among You
parts.epigraph: I will walk among you, and will be your God, and you will be my people.

parts.title: Part Three · Bless You and Keep You
parts.epigraph: Yahweh bless you, and keep you.

parts.title: Part Four · Has His Hand Grown Short?
Part Five · A Star Out of Jacob
parts.epigraph: A star will come out of Jacob.

paintings.title: called
paintings.poem:
the book begins
with a voice
from inside a tent.

not from the mountain now,
with thunder and smoke,

but from a tent
pitched in the middle
of the camp,

among the cooking fires
and the washing
and the children.

everything that follows,
every rule about fire and flour,

is an answer
to one question:

how do people like us
come near?

paintings.title: a pleasant aroma
paintings.poem:
smoke going up
in a straight line
on a still morning.

the whole camp
could see it
from their tent doors.

something given away
completely,
turned to fire and air,

and heaven
called it
pleasant.

you might think
what you give up
simply disappears.

it doesn't.
it rises.

paintings.title: salt
paintings.poem:
fine flour.
a little oil.
a pinch of frankincense.

and never
forget the salt.

salt doesn't spoil.
it keeps things.

so every small gift,
even a handful of flour,

was seasoned
with a reminder:

this is not a deal
that goes bad.

this is a promise
that keeps.

paintings.title: a fifth part more
paintings.poem:
if you took it,
give it back.

if you lied about
what you found,
return it.

and then,
before you go
to the altar,

add a fifth.

not just enough
to make it even.

a little more,
so your neighbor knows
you meant it.

paintings.title: it shall not go out
paintings.poem:
every morning
someone got up
before the others

and fed it.

a few pieces of wood.
nothing grand.

no one ever saw
the fire lit.
only the fire kept.

that's most of faith,
really.

not the flash
from heaven.

the wood,
every morning,
laid on the coals.

paintings.title: ashes
paintings.poem:
the priest
in his linen clothes
swept up the ashes.

then changed
into plain ones

and carried them
out of the camp
to a clean place.

even the leftovers
of holy things
were handled with care.

no one
is too important
to carry the ashes.

and nothing
you gave to God
is thrown away.

paintings.title: hands lifted
paintings.poem:
after all the washing
and the waiting
and the careful fire,

Aaron came down
and lifted up his hands
toward the people.

and then
the glory came.

fire from before the Lord,
and the whole crowd
shouting,
falling on their faces.

it all ends
with a blessing.

that's what
the altar was for.

paintings.title: holy
paintings.poem:
holy
doesn't mean
far away.

it means
set apart,

the way you set apart
the good cup,
the one you keep
for someone you love.

God said,
be holy, as I am.

not,
stay away.

more like,
come be mine.

paintings.title: the living bird
paintings.poem:
the priest
went outside the camp
to find him.

the one who had lived
out there,
away from everyone.

he looked him over,
and the sickness was gone.

and at the end
of the washing,

a bird
was let go
into the open field.

you can go home now.

you are clean.
you are free.

paintings.title: within the veil
paintings.poem:
once a year
one man in plain linen
went behind the curtain

with coals
and two handfuls of incense.

the smoke
covered the mercy seat
like a cloud.

the closest anyone came
to God

was wrapped
in sweetness
and mercy.

paintings.title: into the wilderness
paintings.poem:
two hands
on a goat's head.
every wrong
named out loud.

then someone led it
past the last tent
and let it go.

it walked
into the desert
and didn't come back.

that's where
your sin went.

not coming back.

paintings.title: the corners of the field
paintings.poem:
don't cut
all the way to the edge.

don't go back
for what you dropped.

don't pick up
the grapes
that fell.

leave them.

someone is coming
later in the day
with an empty basket.

God built
a little room
into your harvest

for people
you've never met.

paintings.title: as yourself
paintings.poem:
it's here first,
in the middle
of a long list

about wages
and weights
and gossip
and the deaf and the blind.

don't carry a grudge.
don't get even.

love your neighbor
as yourself.

and further down the page,
the stranger too,

because you knew
what it was like
to be one.

paintings.title: the land shall rest
paintings.poem:
six years
you plow.

the seventh,
you don't.

the vine
goes wild.
the field
grows what it likes.

and everyone eats
from it,
the servant and the stranger
and the animals too.

even the dirt
gets a Sabbath.

God is not
in a hurry
to use anything up.

paintings.title: jubilee
paintings.poem:
every fiftieth year
a horn
across the whole land.

the field you sold
comes back.

the debt
is gone.

the one who had to work
for his neighbor

walks home
with his children.

the land is mine,
God said.

no one
loses everything
forever.

paintings.title: I will walk among you
paintings.poem:
after all the fire
and the rules
and the careful distance,

this.

not
I will watch you.

not
I will visit sometimes.

I will walk
among you.

down the rows of tents.
past your door.

the whole book
was leading here.

paintings.title: one by one
paintings.poem:
the book of Numbers
begins with names.

not a guess.
not a crowd.

name after name,
family after family,

one by one.

you may feel
like a number.

but in this book
every number
was a name first.

paintings.title: around the tent
paintings.poem:
every tribe
had its place,

every family
its banner,

and every tent door
faced the same center.

in the middle
of all that dust
and noise and marching,

a tent
where God lived.

wherever they went,
they set it up first.

and set
their own tents
around it.

paintings.title: bless and keep
paintings.poem:
God gave the priests
their words.

this is how
you bless my people.

say it like this.

he didn't leave it
to chance.

he didn't
let them guess.

he wanted them
to hear
exactly this:

bless you.
keep you.

paintings.title: his face
paintings.poem:
not his hand
raised against you.

not his back
turned.

his face.

shining.

lifted
toward you.

and at the end
of the blessing,
the thing he wants you
to leave with:

peace.

paintings.title: seven lamps
paintings.poem:
the lamps
were turned
to shine forward.

not up
at the gold.

not back
at the one
who lit them.

out,
into the room.

a light
is not for looking at.

it's for seeing by.

paintings.title: cloud and fire
paintings.poem:
by day
a cloud.

by night
a glow like fire.

a child
could step out of her tent
at midnight

and look
toward the middle of the camp

and see it
still there.

he didn't leave
when it got dark.

he doesn't now.

paintings.title: a month, or a year
paintings.poem:
sometimes one night.
sometimes a month.
sometimes a whole year
in the same dry place.

when the cloud stayed,
they stayed.
when it moved,
they moved.

some seasons
the faithful thing
is to unpack.

paintings.title: a resting place
paintings.poem:
the ark
went out ahead.

three days
ahead of them.

looking
for a place
where they could rest.

you're not
the first one
down this road.

he went ahead
to find
somewhere you can stop.

paintings.title: the dew
paintings.poem:
every night
while they slept

it came down
with the dew.

small and pale
like coriander seed.

they ground it,
boiled it,
baked it into cakes.

it tasted
like fresh oil.

every morning
enough.

every morning
again.

paintings.title: we remember the fish
paintings.poem:
the cucumbers.
the melons.
the leeks, the onions, the garlic.

funny how
you can remember
every vegetable

and forget
the whip.

nothing at all
but this manna,
they said,

holding
bread from heaven
in their hands.

be careful
what you call
nothing.

paintings.title: not alone
paintings.poem:
it's too heavy,
Moses said.

I can't carry them
alone.

and God
didn't tell him
to try harder.

he said,
gather seventy.

and took
of the Spirit
that was on Moses
and put it on them.

sometimes
the answer to your prayer
is other people.

paintings.title: very humble
paintings.poem:
his own sister and brother
spoke against him.

he didn't answer back.
God did.

and when Miriam
was shut outside the camp,
Moses was the one who cried,
heal her.

and the whole people
waited seven days
until she was
brought back in.

paintings.title: Eshcol
paintings.poem:
one cluster of grapes
so big

it took
two men
and a pole.

and pomegranates.
and figs.

forty days in the land,
and this is what
they carried home.

proof.

every good thing
God had promised

was hanging
right there
between them.

paintings.title: grasshoppers
paintings.poem:
twelve went.
twelve saw
the same fruit,
the same walls.

ten came back
and said,
we were like grasshoppers.

Caleb said,
let's go up at once.

same land.
same giants.

the difference
wasn't what they saw.

it was
who they thought
was going with them.

paintings.title: the rod that budded
paintings.poem:
twelve dry sticks
left overnight
in the tent.

in the morning
one of them
was a tree.

buds,
blossoms,
and ripe almonds,

all at once,
on wood
cut and dry
and lying still.

God chooses
by making
something live.

paintings.title: abundantly
paintings.poem:
the people were quarreling.
Moses was angry.

he was told
to speak to the rock,
and he struck it twice.

and still
the water came.
not a trickle.
abundantly.

Moses paid a price that day.
but God did not let
the people go thirsty.

paintings.title: look and live
paintings.poem:
they were tired and angry,
and the desert
was full of snakes.

God did not
take the desert away.

he gave them
something to look at:
a bronze pole
lifted up where all could see.

no medicine.
no climbing.

turn your eyes,
and live.

paintings.title: spring up, well
paintings.poem:
this time
no one complained.

God said,
gather the people,
I will give them water.

and they sang
to a hole in the ground.

spring up.

paintings.title: the donkey
paintings.poem:
three times
she turned aside.

three times
he struck her.

he thought
she was being stubborn.

she was
saving his life.

the only one
on that road
who could see the angel

was the donkey.

be slow to hit
what's stopping you.

paintings.title: I can't reverse it
paintings.poem:
a king
paid a prophet
to curse them.

three times
he climbed a mountain.

three times
he opened his mouth,

and blessing
came out instead.

no one
can hire
a curse on you

strong enough
to undo
what God
has already said.

paintings.title: but not near
paintings.poem:
from the top of a hill
a man who came to curse
saw a star.

not now.
not near.

far off,
rising
out of Jacob.

some promises
you only see
from a distance.

the star
was still coming.

paintings.title: the daughters speak right
paintings.poem:
Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah,
Milcah, Tirzah.

five sisters
with no brother
and no share of the land.

they stood at the door of the tent,
in front of everyone,
and asked.

Moses brought it to God.

and God said,
they're right,

and wrote it into the law
for every daughter after them.

paintings.title: a shepherd
paintings.poem:
told he would not
go into the land,

Moses didn't argue
for himself.

he prayed
for them.

give them someone
to go out before them
and bring them in.

don't leave them
like sheep
with no shepherd.

then he laid his hands
on Joshua

and let go.

paintings.title: cities of refuge
paintings.poem:
even in the law
there was a door
left open.

six towns,
three on each side
of the Jordan,

for the one
who never meant it,
running,
with nowhere else to go.

get inside,
and you are safe.

the long road
ends with a place
to run to.
